title: A-MEM — where the paper and the upstream code part ways
subtitle: Only paper ↔ upstream-code divergences are drawn (memory-bench's fixed arm is a separate comparison, not shown here). Each node states both sides.
source: paper arXiv:2502.12110v11  ×  repo agiresearch/A-mem @ ceffb86   ·   servers/amem/verification.md §5.1, 13 paper↔upstream divergences (D1-D13)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ upstream-code divergence
legend_notes: The headline (hardest evidence in this recheck): note construction (Eq.2) never runs — analyze_content() has one call site in the whole repo, its own def. Every note's semantic fields sit at fallback defaults, indistinguishable from a successful call from outside.

Every LLM-driven semantic mechanism the paper names — construct, link, evolve — is broken in a different way in code; only the deterministic plumbing (persist, index, deliver) matches the paper's shape.
D9 ties a paper-side promise to a code-side silence: Fig.2's caption implies linked memories are kept, but the code computes them and then return memories[:k] throws away all of them.

D13 is a probable mislabel in verification.md's own table (tagged paper-only there): the fields in question exist only in the code, so this spec draws it as code_only — flagged for the parent session.
